dedupe_keys.name: nismod lp long term strategic infrastructure planning model for saint lucia

description: This Excel model encodes the analytical steps of a National Infrastructure Systems Modelling (NISMOD-LP) application for Saint Lucia, developed through a partnership between the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) and the UK Infrastructure Transitions Research Consortium led by the University of Oxford. It supported the country's first national infrastructure assessment (2020) and covers six stages: the structure and function of current infrastructure systems, future needs under three demand scenarios driven by population, tourism and climate change, visions for future development, strategic alternatives (capacity expansion, system efficiency and restructuring), performance of those strategies across sectors, and adaptive pathways of investments and policies. Sectors include energy, water, wastewater and solid waste, and input cells are marked in red so users can update data. It was built by Daniel Adshead, Orlando Roman, Scott Thacker, Fabian Felix, Lena Fuldauer and Adrian Hickford, and version 1.0.0 was released on Zenodo on 4 June 2021 as a single Excel workbook under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: current-system data come mostly from public sources, uncertainty in inputs carries through, and sector scope is limited by data availability. It supports capacity planning and climate adaptation pathways for small island states; a related record is the infrastructure climate resilience data starter kits from the same Oxford group.
